blocks.text: *The setting, the artist's unfinished book, and why the world looks the way it does.*

An artist wrote a story in a book and drew its pictures himself — a gentle, peaceful story. Everything he finished is on the page, **drawn flat**. Everyone he has only imagined so far is **unwritten**: real in his mind, not yet on the page.

But unwanted thoughts kept breaking into his mind, and the pictures there grew chaotic. Those thoughts took one shape and one name: **Chaos**. Chaos lives only inside the artist's mind, and it has tried again and again to wreck his peace and his book. It never erases what he wrote — it **corrupts** it.
The world is called *Unwritten* for the people still waiting to be written — and you are one of them.

To fight Chaos the artist imagined fourteen champions, the **Fourteen Kashira**. Together they sealed it away — but not before it **corrupted pages of the book**, twisting the characters drawn on them into monsters.

After the battles the artist grew **paranoid**: what if Chaos had infected the Fourteen before it was sealed? He thought it until, in his mind, it became true. Chaos's power spread evenly through the fourteen, and they turned — the **fourteen shadows**. Now only the unwritten stand with him. You are one of them, and your task is to end that fear: restore the corrupted pages, and in the end face the shadows.
Nothing about how Unwritten looks is arbitrary. The visual style *is* the story:

items: **The flat, papery monsters are corrupted pages.** They are literally paper — drawings Chaos twisted. Their flatness isn't an art choice; it's what they are.

**The colorless, charcoal heroes are the unwritten.** The body is 3D and fully present, but the artist hasn't put them on the page yet — no color, no self. A faint trace of identity is already there: a hint of colored hair, an inked eye.
**Beating a monster restores its page.** What it drops is what the page gives back.

blocks.text: Progression in Unwritten is the story of **getting your color.** The more of you is written — growing stronger, journeying further, uncovering story, mastering a weapon — the more **color returns to you**, identity arriving for the first time. A fully realized hero is one the artist has written a great deal of.

The Fourteen Kashira were never put on the page, so they have **no names** — only epithets, and **fourteen weapons**. They sealed Chaos away; then the artist's fear turned them into the fourteen shadows.

items: **Each of the fourteen weapons is one of them.** A weapon is what the artist kept of a Kashira from before the fear took them. How the weapon fights *is* how that Kashira fought.
**They are known only by epithet, never by name** — the Shield is *The One Who Stood*, the Dagger is *The Late Arrival*. The missing name is the point, and it is also the reward.

**A weapon teaches its wielder's skills in fragments.** You learn them by fighting with that kind of weapon, a few at a time as your mastery grows — and a weapon forged by a smith carries one of them more strongly than the rest: its **trademark**, the skill it is named for.

**Remembering who they really were frees the artist.** Every Kashira you come to know through their weapon proves to him that Chaos never truly had them. Master whichever weapons you like — nobody has to learn all fourteen.
**Carrying one bleeds their identity into you** — this is the charcoal-to-color return. You are not recovering *the* truth; you are finishing *a* story.
**Naming a Kashira is the endgame.** Learn enough of a weapon's skills and its true name can finally be written down — fourteen names to write, fourteen journeys to finish.

rows: Met every challenge alone, one at a time, and never lost the exchange.
The One Who Cleared the Road
Walked ahead of the others so there would be a path behind.
Would not be turned, would not defend, only pressed forward.
Whatever the enemy meant to do, it did not get to.
The One Who Moved the Line
Decided where everyone stood, on both sides.
Took what was meant for the other thirteen.
Was never where the blow landed, and never out of range.
Was not in the fight until it was already ending.
Needed one shot; waited as long as that took.
The One Who Burned the Field
Unmade the ground the enemy was standing on.
The One Who Brought Them Back
Is the reason the other thirteen were still standing.
Did nothing quickly, and nothing survived it.

blocks.text: The great powers of the world

items: **Chaos** — the unwanted thoughts in the artist's mind, sealed away by the Fourteen. It never erases; it corrupts.
**The fourteen shadows** — the Kashira, turned by the artist's fear. Chaos's power is split evenly between them.
**The corrupted pages** — the monsters of the world, and the reason to keep walking.
